Anya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal for a lightweight "staged migration" model.
Anya: TL;DR: introduce a small staging window in host memory with migration cost scoring so we can avoid expensive synchronous evicts during busy traffic.
Sam: Can you outline how this differs from existing 'host staging pool' we have today?
Anya: Existing pool is a blunt pool: pages either in resident GPU or moved to host backing. New idea: ephemeral staging window (ms to seconds) with probabilistic residency retention and a cost model per allocation.
Derek: Interested. How do we compute "migration cost"? I assume bandwidth + stall penalty + eviction churn?
Anya: Yep. Score = estimated memcpy bytes / available bw + tail-latency penalty if we block on migration + expected reuse probability.
Rachael: Expected reuse probability needs historical signal. Are we keeping per-allocation counters? That could be heavy.
Anya: Not per-allocation counters. We bucket by model layer and allocation class, keep exponential decay counters. Lightweight sketches.
Sam: Ok. How does allocator API change? We don't want app code to be full of heuristics.
Anya: Add two new ops: reserve_token(metadata) -> token and promote(token) / demote(token). Reserve indicates intent to use soon; allocator attaches a score and a soft residency hint. Promote forces GPU residency if score high enough.
Derek: Example flow?
Anya: Code:
```
// model runtime
tok = allocator.reserve_token(size, {layer:"attn_kv", expected_seq:128})
// infer path sees many prompt tokens
if (will_execute) allocator.promote(tok)
```
Sam: Where does the migrator live? Kernel thread in runtime or separate service?
Anya: Separate migrator thread per GPU host. It consumes tokens with low score and stages them into host window. Evictions are async, but migrator can accelerate critical promotes.
Rachael: What about fragmentation of the staging window itself? If it's small we can get lots of churn.
Anya: Two mitigations: (1) slabized subpools for common allocation sizes, (2) prefactor that buys extra staging quota for allocations with high reuse score.
Derek: Does this interact with QUOTA / tenant fairness?
Anya: Yes — tokens include tenant id and an adjustable eviction penalty; migrator picks victims by per-tenant score to avoid unfair eviction.
Sam: Any telemetry we should add?
Anya: Token lifecycle metrics (reserve -> promote -> demote -> evict), migration latency histogram, per-bucket reuse rate, and per-tenant staging footprint.
Rachael: Migration backpressure on PCIe is a concern. Does migrator throttle based on BW? We should also tie to host IO util.
Anya: Migrator does adaptive rate limiting based on measured memcpy throughput and inferred queueing delay.
Derek: Sounds promising. My main worry: complexity of tokens leaking and memory accounting bugs.
Anya: Agreed. Plan: phased rollout - start with advisory tokens (no hard promote), then enable async migrator + metrics, then promote. Also add GC for stale tokens after TTL.
Sam: Can you open a short RFC doc with state machine and metrics? I'll review.
Anya: Yep — https://rfc.internal/s/staged-migration (WIP) 
Rachael: :+1: 
evict-bot: migrator: scheduled compaction pass started (node=gpu3)
Sam: Thanks — will sync in eng-runtime sync tomorrow.
Anya: Thanks all.
